subject: Concordia + Redwood: SDK co-delivery & telemetry hooks SOW
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@concordia.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Concordia + Redwood: SDK co-delivery & telemetry hooks SOW

Hi Diego —

Great to meet you at KubeCon last week. Concordia is moving ahead with a modular SDK for customers that wraps LangChain and LlamaIndex patterns; we'd like Redwood to be our official inference partner and to co-deliver an "instrumentation shim" that surfaces prompt-level telemetry into our analytic pipelines. Key asks from our side: 

- A lightweight adapter that lets LangChain/LlamaIndex users route calls to Redwood runtime (including model variants + fallback) with minimal code changes.
- Prompt/response tracing (prompt template id, token counts, model variant, latency, errors) emitted to our telemetry endpoint and optionally to OpenTelemetry.
- An integration checklist and a short pilot SOW (2–3 sprints) with clear deliverables and acceptance criteria.

We're targeting an internal pilot with three customers in Q3. Can you share a quick SOW and an availability window for a kickoff? Marcus from ForgeVA (cc'd) will co-deliver on engineering and will handle some of the instrumentation work.

Attachments: none on this ping — just wanted to get the ball rolling.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Partnerships
Concordia Analytics
lena@concordia.ai
+1 (415) 555-0197

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Concordia + Redwood: SDK co-delivery & telemetry hooks SOW

Lena —

Thanks — excited to explore this. We (Redwood) have a few established patterns for SDK integrations but want to scope this to Concordia's needs. A couple of clarifying questions before I put a draft SOW together: 

1) Which LangChain/LlamaIndex versions do your customers predominantly use? Are you expecting to support both the Python and Typescript SDKs?
2) For telemetry, do you want Redwood to push events directly to Concordia's OTLP endpoint, or emit records to a message bus (Kafka) that your pipeline will consume?
3) Any non-negotiable security/compliance constraints (e.g., no token logging, required field redaction) we should account for in the SOW?

We can run a 45-minute technical kickoff next week — Wed/Thu AM PST works for me. Looping in Karthik (runtime integrations) and Vanessa (partners) to help draft the SOW and resource-plan.

Proposed next step: I’ll share a 1-page scope + draft SOW and a 2-sprint timeline by EOD tomorrow if that works.

— Diego Fernandez
Sr. Partnerships Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.ai

Lena / Marcus —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a short pilot SOW (Concordia-Redwood-SOW-v1.pdf) and an instrumentation example (instrumentation_patch.diff) that shows how we propose to surface the following events: prompt.template_id, prompt.hash, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, error_code.

High-level summary (SOW v1):
- Sprint 0 (week 1): design & security review; establish OTLP and test sandbox; define redaction rules.
- Sprint 1 (week 2–3): implement Python LangChain adapter + telemetry hooks; unit tests + integration test harness.
- Sprint 2 (week 4–5): Typescript adapter (LangChain/LLM wrappers) + pilot onboarding for customer A; create integration-checklist.xlsx and runbook.

Acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end demo: Concordia sees sanitized traces in their OTLP endpoint for 10 canonical prompts.
2) No token or PII leakage: automated test shows redaction rules applied.
3) Packaging & docs: python package + npm package, integration guide, and checklist delivered.

Security/compliance notes:
- By default we will not log full prompt text unless explicitly enabled by the customer. The default is prompt.template_id + masked prompt hash.
- All keys will be proxied through Redwood's Key Management layer in the private pilot.

Deliverables attached: Concordia-Redwood-SOW-v1.pdf, instrumentation_patch.diff, integration-checklist.xlsx, design-diagram.png

Estimated staffing: 2 Redwood engineers (one runtime, one SDK), 1 ForgeVA engineer, 0.5 PM + 0.3 security reviewer. Total estimated effort: 6–8 engineer-weeks.

Next steps:
- Please review SOW + instrumentation examples and confirm approval.
- If approved, sign the DocuSign link below (we'll fill in the procurement details) and we'll schedule a technical kickoff on Tue Jun 29 10:00 AM PST.
